title: Which objects around us have rotational symmetry?
description: The fan, the flower and the wheel of the book are tested by imagining a turn about the centre. An object counts when it looks the same after a turn less than the full turn. Keeko's doubt is that the butterfly has rotational symmetry because it looks balanced.
teaching_notes: One idea: look for equal parts round a centre and test with a turn less than the full turn. Watch for students who say an object has rotational symmetry just because it looks balanced.

source: Like wheels, we can find other objects around us having rota
video_script.why: The child learns how to look for rotational symmetry in objects, by finding equal parts round a centre and testing a turn.
video_script.substitution: the book's fan, flower and wheel, each turned about its centre
video_script.anchor: the book's fan, flower and wheel, each with a dot at its centre
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says the butterfly has rotational symmetry because it looks balanced.
video_script.payoff_line: Objects that look the same after a turn less than the full turn have rotational symmetry

final_answer.value: Open ended: objects that look the same after a turn less than 360°, such as a fan, a flower with equal petals, a wheel with equal spokes
final_answer.spoken: objects that look the same after a turn less than the full turn, such as a fan, a flower with equal petals, and a wheel with equal spokes

hold_back: objects that look the same after a turn less than 360°
maths_rules: look for equal parts round a centre
test by turning about the centre; the turn must be less than 360°, because every object fits after 360°
a fan with 3 equal blades fits after 360 ÷ 3 = 120°
a flower with 5 equal petals fits after 360 ÷ 5 = 72°
a wheel with equal spokes fits after the turn from one spoke to the next
the butterfly does not fit after a half turn, since its head would be at the bottom
video_script.design: The fan, the flower and the wheel from the book, each with equal parts round a centre. A turn less than the full turn is tested on each. Keeko's doubt is that the butterfly looks balanced and so must have rotational symmetry.
open_questions: The question is open ended. The fan is taken to have three equal blades and the flower five equal petals, as the book's pictures are described in the worklist, since the extracted book text has no pictures.
